explanation: The first and last houses cannot both be robbed. Run the linear recurrence once excluding the last and once excluding the first, taking the larger result. Handle a singleton separately.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for n houses. Two scans of at most n-1 houses remain O(n) total.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. Each linear run retains two prefix totals and index bounds.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 C++ algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Any legal selection in a cycle excludes at least one of the adjacent first and last houses. Selections excluding the last are covered by the first linear run, and selections excluding the first by the second. Each run is optimal for its case; taking their maximum therefore covers every legal cyclic selection.
walkthrough: For [8,2,3,9], the linear choice 8+9 is forbidden because the endpoints are neighbors. Excluding the last permits 8+3=11; excluding the first permits 2+9=11. The larger valid total is 11.
edgeCases: A singleton is handled separately so it is not excluded from both runs.
First and last houses cannot both be selected.
Either endpoint may be skipped; both may also be skipped.
